'''Đuro Kurepa''' ([[Serbian Cyrillic alphabet|Serbian Cyrillic]]: Ђуро Курепа, {{IPA|sh|dʑǔːro kǔrepa|pron}}; 16 August 1907 – 2 November 1993) was a Yugoslav and [[Serbs |Serbian]] [[mathematician]], university professor and academic.<ref name="emis"/>

Throughout his life, Kurepa published over 700 articles, books, papers, and reviews<ref name="mcs">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Kurepa}}</ref> and over 1,000 scientific reviews. He lectured at universities across Europe, as well as those in Canada, Cuba, Iraq, Israel, and the United States, and was quoted saying "I lectured at almost each of [the] nineteen universities of [the former] [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]..."<ref name="emis"/>

==Early life==
Born as '''Đurađ Kurepa''' in [[Majske Poljane]], [[Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia]], [[Austria-Hungary]] to a [[Serbs |Serb]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Srpsko Narodno Vijeće :: Đuro Kurepa |url=https://snv.hr/znameniti-srbi-u-hrvatskoj/djuro-kurepa |access-date=2020-07-16 |website=snv.hr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200716190608/https://snv.hr/znameniti-srbi-u-hrvatskoj/djuro-kurepa |archive-date=16 July 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> family. In English, his name was transliterated as '''Djuro Kurepa''' while in French he is often attributed as '''Georges Kurepa'''. Kurepa was the youngest of Rade and Anđelija Kurepa's fourteen children. His nephew was the mathematician [[Svetozar Kurepa]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/znanost-it/umro-istaknuti-matematicar-svetozar-kurepa.html|title=Umro istaknuti matematičar Svetozar Kurepa|access-date=2010-05-30|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083326/http://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/znanost-it/umro-istaknuti-matematicar-svetozar-kurepa.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

He began his schooling in Majske Poljane, continued his education in Glina, and graduated from high school in [[Križevci, Croatia|Križevci]].<ref name="mcs"/> He received a diploma in theoretical mathematics and physics from the [[University of Zagreb]] in 1931, and began work as an assistant in the teaching of mathematics the same year. Kurepa then went to the [[Collège de France]] and the [[University of Paris]], where he received his doctoral diploma in 1935; his advisor was French mathematician [[Maurice René Fréchet]], and his thesis was titled ''Ensembles ordonnés et ramifiés''.<ref name="mcs"/>

==Career==
Kurepa continued to receive post-doctoral education at [[Warsaw University]] in [[Poland]] and the University of Paris. He became an assistant professor at the University of Zagreb in 1937, associate professor the next year, and assumed the position of full professor in 1948.<ref name="emis"/> After the end of [[World War II]] and the formation of the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]], he traveled to five universities in the United States: [[Harvard University]] in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Massachusetts]], the [[University of Chicago]] in [[Chicago, Illinois|Chicago]], [[Illinois]], the branch of the [[University of California]] at [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]] and the branch at [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]], [[New Jersey]]<ref name="mcs"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/djuro-kurepa |title=IAS Member: Djuro Kurepa (Mathematics) |access-date=2018-01-04 |archive-date=2018-01-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105123131/https://www.ias.edu/scholars/djuro-kurepa |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Columbia University]] in [[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]].<ref name="emis"/>

Kurepa was an [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] Plenary Speaker in 1954 and 1958.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897 |access-date=2017-04-23 |archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1965, Kurepa shifted to the [[University of Belgrade]], where he focused on the mathematical fields of [[mathematical logic|logic]] and [[set theory]]. Kurepa was a member of several organizations, including the [[Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts]] and the [[Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts|Yugoslav Academy of Sciences and Arts]].<ref name="hazu">{{cite web| url = http://www.hazu.hr/ENG/Founding.html| title = The Founding of the Academy| access-date = 2007-01-01| date = 2004-12-23| publisher = Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060928085411/http://www.hazu.hr/ENG/Founding.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2006-09-28}}</ref> He was also the founder and president of the Society of Mathematicians and Physicists of Croatia, the founder and chief editor of the journal ''Mathematica Balkanica'', and the president of the Yugoslav National Committee for Mathematics, the Balkan Mathematical Society, and the Union of Yugoslav Societies of Mathematicians, Physicisists and Astronomers. He received the [[AVNOJ Award]] in 1976, and retired from the University of Belgrade in 1977.<ref name="emis"/>

He  published his scientific works in the most notable European and world scientific journals, including: ''[[Mathematische Annalen]], Izvestiya Akademii nauk SSSR, [[Fundamenta Mathematicae]], [[Acta Mathematica]], [[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]], [[Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France]], Zeitschrift für mathematische Logik und Grundlagen der Mathematik, [[Journal of Symbolic Logic]], [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]].''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://banija.rs/banija/14183-poznati-banijci-profesor-djuro-kurepa.html|title=Poznati Banijci: Profesor Đuro Kurepa|website=Banija Online|language=sr-latn-rs|access-date=2022-11-06|archive-date=2022-11-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221106174910/https://banija.rs/banija/14183-poznati-banijci-profesor-djuro-kurepa.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Death and legacy==
On 1 November 1993, Kurepa was robbed and [[Strike (attack)|beaten]] after retrieving his pension from a bank.<ref name="1993 ref">{{cite web |url=http://www.aimpress.ch/dyn/pubs/archive/data/199311/31113-002-pubs-beo.htm |author=Alternativna informativna mreža |title=Nauka ne stanuje više ovde |access-date=2020-08-11 |date=1993-11-13 |language=sr |archive-date=2021-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211231102025/http://www.aimpress.ch/dyn/pubs/archive/data/199311/31113-002-pubs-beo.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He was then hidden from view under a set of stairs.<ref>Sets and Extensions in the Twentieth Century  by Dov M. Gabbay, Akihiro Kanamori (eds.), and John Woods, Elsevier, 2012 p. 186</ref> He succumbed to his injuries on 2 November 1993 in a Belgrade [[emergency department|emergency ward]].<ref name="1993 ref 2">{{cite web |url=http://www.yurope.com/news/mileva/prva/0034.html |author=Radio Mileva #39 |title=Preksinoć u Beogradu |access-date=2022-03-25 |date=1993-11-06 |language=sr |archive-date=2022-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201102039/http://www.yurope.com/news/mileva/prva/0034.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He is interred in the [[Belgrade New Cemetery#Alley of Distinguished Citizens|Alley of Distinguished Citizens]] in the [[Belgrade New Cemetery]].

As a mathematician, he is known especially for his works on set theory and [[general topology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://legati.matf.bg.ac.rs/kurepa/biografija.html|title=Đuro Kurepa|website=legati.matf.bg.ac.rs|access-date=2022-11-06|archive-date=2022-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407182841/http://legati.matf.bg.ac.rs/kurepa/biografija.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kurepa influenced set theory in several ways, including lending his name to the [[Kurepa tree]]. According to Kajetan Šeper, Kurepa's colleague from the University of Zagreb:
<blockquote>
Professor Kurepa was not only the professional mathematician and teacher, but he was a scientist, philosopher, and humanist as well, in the true sense of these words. He was the founder and pioneer in mathematical logic and the foundations of mathematics in Croatia, and modern mathematical theories in Croatia and Yugoslavia. Generally speaking, he was the catalyzer, the initiator, and the bearer of mathematical science.
</blockquote>

According to the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]], Kurepa supervised 27 students, including analytic number theorist [[Aleksandar Ivić]], set theorist [[Stevo Todorčević]] and topologist [[Ljubisa D.R. Kocinac]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ðuro Kurepa|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=24627|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project|access-date=2016-12-15|archive-date=2016-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170240/http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=24627|url-status=live}}</ref>
